subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is referenced as the authority who decides the fate of failed adventurers, with the phrase 'being a dwarf raised by giants means I don’t have to have any range. Giants toss rocks. Those rocks go far and hurt. My job was to be there and protect the giants from anything that came too close.'
source_quote: being a dwarf raised by giants means I don’t have to have any range. Giants toss rocks. Those rocks go far and hurt. My job was to be there and protect the giants from anything that came too close.

subject: Underdark
fact: The Underdark is tight and low, and this is a dangerous world, and we have a dangerous job, and we none of us have ranged weapons, which means there will absolutely be something that needs hitting from a distance.
source_quote: The Underdark is tight and low. But we're almost out. And this is a dangerous world, and we have a dangerous job, and we none of us have ranged weapons, which means there will absolutely be something that needs hitting from a distance.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz made a noise of genuine surprise — the kind he usually reserves for things like demon princes and sentient oozes — and concluded, 'We're gonna level up.'
source_quote: Daz made a noise of genuine surprise — the kind he usually reserves for things like demon princes and sentient oozes. 'Oh!' And then, with that particular tone he uses when he's already processed something and moved to judgment: 'We're gonna level up.'

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir considers most things like he's checking the weight of the stone before deciding where to put it, and states, 'I find it more fun to double down with some sort of obscure specialization and then try to break the universe with it.'
source_quote: Zalthir considered this for a moment in the way he considers most things — like he's checking the weight of the stone before deciding where to put it. 'I find it more fun to double down with some sort of obscure specialization and then try to break the universe with it.'

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is described as someone who builds narrow and builds sharp, everything pointing in one direction, so that in exactly the right situation, he becomes something close to impossible.
source_quote: Something about the way the Dragonborn operated had always impressed me, even when I didn't understand it. He builds narrow and builds sharp. Everything pointing in one direction, so that in exactly the right situation, he becomes something close to impossible.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir pulled the Pudding King out of its lair by sheer force of tactical geometry, demonstrating commitment to a direction and refusal to apologize for it.
source_quote: I'd watched him pull the Pudding King out of its lair by sheer force of tactical geometry. That was a man who had committed to a direction and refused to apologize for it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is described as thinking several steps ahead of everyone else, in some private tactical space behind his eyes, and when asked about strategy, responds with a refined philosophy of focused power.
source_quote: Zalthir looked at me with that particular expression that meant he'd thought four moves ahead already.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir acknowledges the complexity of feat selection with the statement, 'Yeah, this'll take some time.'
source_quote: He said very little, which is Zalthir's preferred mode. Just: 'Feats, huh.' And then, with the considered weight of someone who was not actually complaining but acknowledging a genuine complexity: 'Yeah, this'll take some time.'

subject: Daz
fact: Daz considers Warcaster as an obvious choice for improving concentration checks, noting that it is not decorative but the difference between a spell persisting and dissolving at the wrong moment.
source_quote: Warcaster was the obvious answer, and I noted it without sentiment. If I'm maintaining concentration on a spell worth maintaining — Hypnotic Pattern, Maximilian's Grasp — then the ability to hold that concentration when something lands a hit is not decorative. It is the difference between the spell persisting and the spell dissolving at precisely the wrong moment.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz chooses Fey Touched because it grants two additional prepared spells and free castings, and connects to the spellbook taken from Princess Ebonmire as a door not yet fully opened.
source_quote: Fey Touched gives me two additional spells to prepare. Plus free castings. ... The spellbook we'd taken from Princess Ebonmire had been sitting in my pack like a promissory note I hadn't finished reading. Prepared spells are the real resource for a wizard — not the castings themselves, not the slots, but the selection. What you've loaded before the situation becomes the situation. Fey Touched was a key, and the Ebonmire spellbook was a door I hadn't fully opened yet.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz values Misty Step for its ability to allow escape without incurring attacks of opportunity, especially from grappled situations, due to its free casting.
source_quote: No — being able to cast it without expending a spell slot is extremely useful. Because if you're in combat, it allows you to get out without incurring attacks of opportunity. It allows you to get out of a grappled situation.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz considers Telekinetic as a geometry tool for positioning allies, recognizing that moving Zalthir five feet can be more valuable than a Scorching Ray.
source_quote: Telekinetic, I can aim this at allies and do things like get them out of a grapple. Move them five feet. ... There are situations where moving Zalthir five feet in the right direction is more valuable than a Scorching Ray. He is, when correctly positioned, substantially more dangerous than a Scorching Ray.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz conceives of his spell selection as a system — Sculpt Spells meeting Cloud of Daggers meeting spatial logic — calling it 'the long arrangement' after Milo Goodbarrel.
source_quote: Sculpt Spells lets me carve exclusions into area effects. But the area effects I could now access, combined with the concentration durability Warcaster would provide, combined with the escape utility of free Misty Step — these were not independent features. They were a system. ... Milo Goodbarrel had a chapter about this. He called it 'the long arrangement' — the idea that the fight before the fight, the positioning, the preparation, is actually most of the fight.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz writes down Fey Touched with the quiet satisfaction of a calculation that checks out.
source_quote: Fey Touched. That was the one. I wrote it down with the quiet satisfaction of a calculation that checks out.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recognizes that a grapple solves the problem of Cloud of Daggers by pinning a target in place, ensuring the daggers find them exactly where left.
source_quote: If you hold one in place," Daz said, "the daggers keep finding them." I had been thinking about it too. Cloud of Daggers: a rotating cage of blades, hungry in one fixed point in space. The problem has always been that enemies move. But a grapple — a proper hold, weight-to-weight, the kind that pins something to a specific square of floor — that solved it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir confirms that a grapple keeps the target where placed, but the grappler occupies an adjacent space, so he will not be affected by Daz’s Cloud of Daggers.
source_quote: A grapple keeps the target where I put them, but I am not inside them — I am beside them, adjacent, occupying my own space while they occupy theirs. Daz could put his cloud directly on the grappled target and I would walk away without a scratch.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir understands that grapple is a quick action, but binding with rope consumes the full action, making setup a two-turn process that locks down one enemy for maximum damage.
source_quote: Grapple is a quick thing — one motion, a grab, a test of weight and leverage, done in the space of a heartbeat. That leaves the hands. Rope is slower. Tying something takes focus, takes both hands, takes the better part of a turn spent crouching over a target that is probably trying to bite you. The grapple could happen in the spare moment before my main action. The binding would consume the action itself. The whole turn — both pieces of it — spent on one enemy, pinned to the floor, with Daz's daggers already spinning above them.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recalls a monastery class on battlefield geometry and control vs. proximity, though he cannot remember the instructor, and now learns it from a Drow wizard in a tunnel.
source_quote: I said: there was a class on this. At the monastery. Something about battlefield geometry and the difference between control and proximity. I think it was Brother Heslin — or possibly that was the one who taught falling. I'm genuinely uncertain. Either way, I remember the light through the shuttered window and thinking the form was taking too long. I did not remember what they said. I am currently learning it from a Drow wizard in a tunnel.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is described as having a tactical synergy with Daz, where his grapple enables Daz’s area-of-effect spells to persistently target enemies, forming a coordinated combat system.
source_quote: We talked through the geometry of it. The question was whether I would catch myself in my own trap, whether holding something at arm's length meant I'd be eating Daz's spell alongside whatever I was holding. The answer was no.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir’s approach to combat is described as building narrow and sharp, with every action pointing toward maximum efficiency in the right situation.
source_quote: He builds narrow and builds sharp. Everything pointing in one direction, so that in exactly the right situation, he becomes something close to impossible.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is noted to have a silent, contemplative mode, and when confronted with feat selection, acknowledges its complexity without complaint.
source_quote: He said very little, which is Zalthir's preferred mode. Just: 'Feats, huh.' And then, with the considered weight of someone who was not actually complaining but acknowledging a genuine complexity: 'Yeah, this'll take some time.'

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir’s combat style is described as being about geometry, positioning, and control — not brute force — and he is shown to be deeply attuned to spatial logic.
source_quote: I am currently learning it from a Drow wizard in a tunnel.

subject: Princess Ebonmire's spellbook
fact: The spellbook taken from Princess Ebonmire is described as a promissory note Daz hasn't finished reading, representing additional prepared spells and potential for expansion.
source_quote: The spellbook we'd taken from Princess Ebonmire had been sitting in my pack like a promissory note I hadn't finished reading.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is described as having been trained by Menzoberranzan to read the moment before decision with surgical attention, knowing what he holds before committing to playing it.
source_quote: Menzoberranzan trained me to read that moment with surgical attention. Know what you hold before you commit to playing it.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz has an instinctive and deeply personal objection to being grabbed, which informs his choice of Misty Step and Telekinetic feats.
source_quote: I've been grabbed before. I have an instinctive and deeply personal objection to being grabbed.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is described as someone who has learned battlefield geometry not from formal instruction but from experience in the Underdark, specifically from a Drow wizard.
source_quote: I am currently learning it from a Drow wizard in a tunnel.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir’s strategy involves using grapple and rope to lock down enemies for two full turns, allowing Daz to exploit the immobilized target with Cloud of Daggers.
source_quote: The grapple could happen in the spare moment before my main action. The binding would consume the action itself. The whole turn — both pieces of it — spent on one enemy, pinned to the floor, with Daz's daggers already spinning above them. That was a full turn spent on setup. The next turn, I would be free — and whatever I had tied down would still be there, still bleeding, while I moved to the next problem.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz concludes that Fey Touched is the optimal choice because it synergizes with the Ebonmire spellbook, expands prepared spells, and provides free castings — a system that aligns with his understanding of wizardry as preparation, not slot expenditure.
source_quote: Fey Touched. That was the one. I wrote it down with the quiet satisfaction of a calculation that checks out.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin acknowledges that the potion you don't drink is the potion you die holding, recognizing his own bad habit of hoarding resources.
source_quote: The potion you don't drink is the potion you die holding.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin identifies Zhentarim Tactics as a ruthless, effective, and uncomfortable school of thought that he is considering adopting, acknowledging his own dark transition from a happy-go-lucky kid to someone who understands the Underdark doesn't care who you want to be.
source_quote: There's a school of thought — brutal, efficient, not entirely reputable — that goes by the name Zhentarim Tactics. Ruthless by design. Effective in ways that decent people find uncomfortable. ... The happy-go-lucky kid who went underground expecting something survivable has spent months watching demon lords and eating mushrooms and coming to understand that the Underdark doesn't care what kind of person you want to be.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin admits his strategy of hoarding resources is wrong but says, 'that's just how I roll,' accepting his flawed but authentic nature.
source_quote: Wrong strategy, but that's just how I roll.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin reflects that the game punishes caution and spreading strengths thin, noting that enemies get bigger and damage must grow with them, or you spend your time bouncing off.
source_quote: The honest truth is that the game punishes you for being cautious about this. Spreading your strengths thin feels responsible. Feels dwarvish, maybe — the sensible hedge, the covered flank. But enemies get bigger, and if your damage doesn't grow with them, you spend your time bouncing off.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin concludes that at our level, you need to mean it, and by the time you're facing whatever's waiting on the surface, you'd better be doing something significant every time you swing.
source_quote: At low levels, a solid strike matters. At our level, you need to mean it. By the time you're facing whatever's waiting for us on the surface, you'd better be doing something significant every time you swing.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin recognizes that not having anyone who can reach a flying enemy is going to come back and bite us.
source_quote: Which is also why not having anyone who can reach a flying enemy is going to come back and bite us.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin confirms that Dawnbringer is not slashing, but deals Radiant damage — clean, divine, the kind of light that argues with darkness on a philosophical level.
source_quote: So question, so Dawnbringer is not slashing, right? It's actually… Radiant damage. Confirmed. The blade doesn't cut so much as it burns — clean, divine, the kind of light that argues with darkness on a philosophical level.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin reflects that he is strong, but questions whether pushing to the absolute ceiling is still satisfying, noting diminishing returns.
source_quote: So I am really strong. Should I get stronger? The point stands. You can push to the absolute ceiling and there's a kind of satisfaction in that, but it's diminishing.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin considers drinking a potion of giant strength when it matters rather than investing in permanent strength increases, recognizing this as a new bad habit.
source_quote: The logic: skip the investment, drink the potion of giant strength when it matters. Which — I recognized, even as I thought it — had given me one more bad habit to account for.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin admits to the habit of saving potions for later, knowing it is wrong but accepting it as part of his nature.
source_quote: Okay, so I'm the type, when I adventure, I'm always like, oh, I don't know, I'm gonna save this potion for later, I might need it. I knew it was wrong when I said it. It's always wrong.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin acknowledges that the lessons of hill giants are carried in the shape of every fight he's won, despite their moral ambiguity.
source_quote: The hill giants weren't always good people either, and I carry their lessons in the shape of every fight I've won.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin admits to having had a dark transition — from a hopeful adventurer to someone who has absorbed the harsh truths of the Underdark.
source_quote: I've had what you might call a dark transition. The happy-go-lucky kid who went underground expecting something survivable has spent months watching demon lords and eating mushrooms and coming to understand that the Underdark doesn't care what kind of person you want to be.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin accepts that things can usually be made to work if you're willing to admit what you've already become.
source_quote: It could be made to work. Things can usually be made to work, if you're willing to admit what you've already become.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin recognizes that the honesty he prefers is honesty you can stand behind without flinching, but he has absorbed truths he cannot deny.
source_quote: It would be honest, even. Not the honesty I prefer — I've always liked honesty you can stand behind without flinching — but there are things you absorb down here whether you mean to or not.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin states that the Underdark doesn't care what kind of person you want to be, and that this realization has changed him.
source_quote: The Underdark doesn't care what kind of person you want to be.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin reflects that taking things seriously takes time, and this is why he is still deciding how to be the fighter he is becoming.
source_quote: I knew immediately how long that was going to take. Not because I couldn't decide, but because I take it seriously, and taking things seriously takes time.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin describes the quiet knock inside the chest as the sign of crossing a threshold he didn't notice crossing, and acknowledges he's felt it before after bad fights.
source_quote: Something hit me, as I surveyed the battlefield. Not literally. Though, given how the last several months have gone, that's worth specifying. No, this was the other kind of thing — the quiet knock inside the chest that means you've crossed some threshold you didn't notice crossing. I've felt it before, in the dark, after bad fights.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin states that the body takes stock before the mind does, and that he was bigger somehow, more there.
source_quote: The body takes stock before the mind does. I was bigger somehow. More there.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin concludes that the game punishes caution, and that by the time you're facing the surface, you must mean it — a philosophy that guides his transformation.
source_quote: At low levels, a solid strike matters. At our level, you need to mean it. By the time you're facing whatever's waiting for us on the surface, you'd better be doing something significant every time you swing.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is referenced by himself as the one who ties things to the ground for Daz to cook, and who killed an ettin with his hands, dragging the Pudding King through his own throne room.
source_quote: Zalthir ties things to the ground for Daz to cook

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir has run the tunnels in his head — the distance traveled, the pace, the absence of obvious threats immediately ahead.
source_quote: I had run the tunnels in my head — the distance we had traveled, the pace, the absence of obvious threats immediately ahead.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin mentioned javelins and had acquired some facility with thrown weapons — a Sharpshooter's instinct, trained in, applied to range — and wanted something with reach for the next engagement.
source_quote: Thorin mentioned javelins. He had apparently acquired some facility with thrown weapons — a Sharpshooter's instinct, trained in, applied to range — and he wanted something with reach for the next engagement.

subject: Ember Grapple
fact: The Ember Grapple holds something still until there is nothing left to hold.
source_quote: The Ember Grapple holds something still until there is nothing left to hold.

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard charges in with fire and flash and the announcement of itself.
source_quote: The Ember Vanguard charges in with fire and flash and the announcement of itself.

subject: Ember Grapple
fact: The Ember Grapple is a named entity described as holding something still until there is nothing left to hold.
source_quote: The Ember Grapple.

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a named entity described as charging in with fire and flash and the announcement of itself.
source_quote: The Ember Vanguard charges in with fire and flash and the announcement of itself.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum made a sound.
source_quote: Grygum made a sound.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin said something about 'the Ember Grapple.'
source_quote: Thorin said something about "the Ember Grapple."

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin found the Ember Grapple very funny.
source_quote: Thorin said something about "the Ember Grapple." Someone — possibly Thorin again, possibly Grygum, it is hard to tell when they are both making noise — found this very funny.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir did not correct the name 'Ember Grapple.'
source_quote: I did not correct it. The name was not wrong.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir turned the matter over once, completely, and then put it down.
source_quote: I turned that over the way I turn most things over: once, completely, and then I put it down.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noted the practicality of the Ember Grapple and moved on.
source_quote: I noted it and moved on.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir let the name 'Ember Grapple' settle.
source_quote: I let it settle.

subject: Ember Grapple
fact: The Ember Grapple is possibly the same party described from two different positions in the room as the Ember Vanguard.
source_quote: Both accurate. Possibly the same party described from two different positions in the room.
